title: Learner 01 | Day 001: Files, folders, and the interpreter
body:
# Learner 01 — Day 001: Files, folders, and the interpreter

**Personal sequence:** Learner 01, Day 1 of 182. **180 minutes**, including the common architecture huddle, implementation, individual proof, peer review, and breaks. No extra hidden daily hours.

[Full daily coaching guide](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/python-fastapi-genai-agents-coaching/blob/main/days/day-001.md) · [Your complete issue sequence](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/python-fastapi-genai-agents-coaching/blob/main/ISSUES.md#learner-01)

## Your dedicated Day 001 implementation

**Exact file:** `src/learnforge/core/values/project.py`

**Add or extend:** module values `PROJECT_NAME` and `WELCOME_MESSAGE`

Add the nonblank text value WELCOME_MESSAGE = "Welcome to LearnForge" beside the existing project name. This defines project-owned text; do not print it or add a validator/function before that lesson.

**Why this location:** This is a value boundary: it defines accepted values and rejects invalid local data. It must not import HTTP, storage, or model SDK code.

### Input, output, and state contract

No arguments. Two named str values are available to callers. PROJECT_NAME remains LearnForge. WELCOME_MESSAGE is exactly Welcome to LearnForge. No I/O, mutation after definition, or new error handling. Empty text fails the agreed example; runtime validators are outside Day 001.

### Observable project increment

The six owners extend the existing working welcome flow. When integrated, `python run_demo.py` prints the welcome, project name, stage day-001, the honest implemented capability, the next lesson, and Example: 5. Your code is one distinct necessary part of that result. Keep the previous entry point working until the integrator connects the accepted units.

This first lesson uses provided function bodies as scaffold; learners are not expected to know function/dict mechanics before they are explained. Each learner's independent first proof is a separate tiny Python file that prints a chosen welcome text and the result of 2 + 3. Save it, run it from its folder, and explain saving versus running. Introduce unfamiliar terms beside the values; do not turn this into a framework or validation lesson.

### Step-by-step explanation and why

1. Start with the project's text values and in-memory state; point to the exact files holding them.
2. Follow the workflow into build_status and show how 2 + 3 becomes numeric 5.
3. Follow that unchanged value into the formatter and explain how its screen text is produced.
4. Follow the command's print operation and show why the text becomes visible only when the program runs.
5. Try running a nonexistent filename and explain the interpreter's file error. No new recovery feature is required.

### Scope and research hints

Only your named unit and this visible first increment are in scope. No input loop, file persistence, classes, API, model call, new test suite, or API documentation. Search Python run a script, Python print text and arithmetic, and Python saving versus executing a file. Predict the output before running it. The supplied scaffold can be explained fully, step by step, without requiring future syntax mastery today.

## One architecture topic — all six together

**Separate stored instructions from a running process. A stopped process cannot remember yesterday's variables.**

Attend the same project-level discussion as the other five learners. Compare options, agree one decision, then implement its effect in your owned slice. Facilitator: Learner 01. Record one shared decision, not six separate architectures. You must personally explain the invariant, failure, and trade-off.

## Your concept proof and Question of the Day

Create a small independent proof in `practice/learner-01/day-001/` using today's concept, including the part implemented by another role. Predict one normal output and one fresh changed case before running it. Use your own values; do not copy a peer's answer. Read the full guide for the short concept explanation, pitfalls, two-question quiz, coding drill, and coach-key link.

**Question of the Day (baseline diagnostic):** Baseline diagnostic, not assumed prior learning: what do you think happens when a program runs? If you have never coded, describe the input and output of a simple calculator.

Explain an example, then answer a changed assumption. In the final stage also explain the data, relevant mathematics, baseline, and failure case of your chosen AI/ML topic. Individual weak areas receive a small targeted repair recorded in your ledger; a peer's pass does not replace yours.

## Your peer-review responsibility

Review **Learner 02's Day 001 implementation**. Their sequence is in the [issue index](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/python-fastapi-genai-agents-coaching/blob/main/ISSUES.md#learner-02). The rotation covers every other learner over five days. Review behavior and the agreed architecture first, then clarity and one relevant edge case. Explain the concept behind a finding; the owner makes the fix. Respond to the peer reviewing your work.

## Light checking and visible integration

Run a small behavior example plus existing relevant checks. Learn or revisit one short testing pattern when relevant; no testing-only task, dedicated tester, coverage quota, or large test suite. Demonstrate your slice connected to the working product, with honest partial/failure outcomes. Keep the last working flow available.

## Implementation acceptance

- [ ] My named owned unit meets the original input/output, error, validation-order, and mutation contract.
- [ ] Its relevant normal/failure examples work in the integrated product.
- [ ] I reviewed the assigned peer, responded to implementation findings, and recorded the actual revision/checks and their limits.

Close this implementation issue when that bounded work is accepted. Follow your own previous-day issue chain; a later task is not a substitute for a missing predecessor. Do not auto-close another learner's issue.

## Separate personal learning record

- My concept proof and explanation:
- Original Question-of-the-Day answer and corrected follow-up:
- Shared architecture understanding:
- Correct / partial / incorrect / missing parts and next repair:
- Chosen AI/ML baseline, mathematics, and evidence when applicable:

Preserve original answers and track understanding independently. A missing learning answer alone does not block a correct PR, and answering must not require extra learner-written tests or documentation. Actual defects against the original contract remain implementation findings. Final mastery/interview readiness needs personal evidence across all common domains and the chosen topic. GitHub assignees remain empty until real accounts are known.


**Micro-detail preview:** reading the provided module text values inside a function does not require a global statement. Do not add one here. Explain this with the coach; full reading/rebinding/mutation rules are taught in Day 012 and revisited through scenarios.
architecture_topic: Separate stored instructions from a running process. A stopped process cannot remember yesterday's variables.
placement_reason: This is a value boundary: it defines accepted values and rejects invalid local data. It must not import HTTP, storage, or model SDK code.

# Learner 06 — Day 001: Files, folders, and the interpreter

**Personal sequence:** Learner 06, Day 1 of 182. **180 minutes**, including the common architecture huddle, implementation, individual proof, peer review, and breaks. No extra hidden daily hours.

[Full daily coaching guide](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/python-fastapi-genai-agents-coaching/blob/main/days/day-001.md) · [Your complete issue sequence](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/python-fastapi-genai-agents-coaching/blob/main/ISSUES.md#learner-06)

## Your dedicated Day 001 implementation

**Exact file:** `src/learnforge/experience/workflows/welcome.py`

**Add or extend:** existing `welcome_status()` plus new small `run_welcome()`

Keep welcome_status as the assembler of project name, starter state, and build_status. Add the small run_welcome entry operation that obtains this status, asks show_status to display it once, and returns the status for inspection. This connects the owners' units without copying their rules.

**Why this location:** This coordinates ordered steps and resource lifetime: orchestration calls the agreed operations/adapters and handles progress/cleanup without copying their rules.

### Input, output, and state contract

run_welcome takes no arguments and returns the status dict it displayed. The state/calculation/display calls occur once in that order; there is no network/file I/O or retry. Reuse welcome_status. After your unit is ready, Learner 01 as integrator switches the thin shared cli.py entry point to call run_welcome; nobody else edits that shared file.

### Observable project increment

The six owners extend the existing working welcome flow. When integrated, `python run_demo.py` prints the welcome, project name, stage day-001, the honest implemented capability, the next lesson, and Example: 5. Your code is one distinct necessary part of that result. Keep the previous entry point working until the integrator connects the accepted units.

This first lesson uses provided function bodies as scaffold; learners are not expected to know function/dict mechanics before they are explained. Each learner's independent first proof is a separate tiny Python file that prints a chosen welcome text and the result of 2 + 3. Save it, run it from its folder, and explain saving versus running. Introduce unfamiliar terms beside the values; do not turn this into a framework or validation lesson.

### Step-by-step explanation and why

1. Start with the project's text values and in-memory state; point to the exact files holding them.
2. Follow the workflow into build_status and show how 2 + 3 becomes numeric 5.
3. Follow that unchanged value into the formatter and explain how its screen text is produced.
4. Follow the command's print operation and show why the text becomes visible only when the program runs.
5. Try running a nonexistent filename and explain the interpreter's file error. No new recovery feature is required.

### Scope and research hints

Only your named unit and this visible first increment are in scope. No input loop, file persistence, classes, API, model call, new test suite, or API documentation. Search Python run a script, Python print text and arithmetic, and Python saving versus executing a file. Predict the output before running it. The supplied scaffold can be explained fully, step by step, without requiring future syntax mastery today.

## One architecture topic — all six together

**Separate stored instructions from a running process. A stopped process cannot remember yesterday's variables.**

Attend the same project-level discussion as the other five learners. Compare options, agree one decision, then implement its effect in your owned slice. Facilitator: Learner 01. Record one shared decision, not six separate architectures. You must personally explain the invariant, failure, and trade-off.

## Your concept proof and Question of the Day

Create a small independent proof in `practice/learner-06/day-001/` using today's concept, including the part implemented by another role. Predict one normal output and one fresh changed case before running it. Use your own values; do not copy a peer's answer. Read the full guide for the short concept explanation, pitfalls, two-question quiz, coding drill, and coach-key link.

**Question of the Day (baseline diagnostic):** Baseline diagnostic, not assumed prior learning: what do you think happens when a program runs? If you have never coded, describe the input and output of a simple calculator.

Explain an example, then answer a changed assumption. In the final stage also explain the data, relevant mathematics, baseline, and failure case of your chosen AI/ML topic. Individual weak areas receive a small targeted repair recorded in your ledger; a peer's pass does not replace yours.

## Your peer-review responsibility

Review **Learner 01's Day 001 implementation**. Their sequence is in the [issue index](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/python-fastapi-genai-agents-coaching/blob/main/ISSUES.md#learner-01). The rotation covers every other learner over five days. Review behavior and the agreed architecture first, then clarity and one relevant edge case. Explain the concept behind a finding; the owner makes the fix. Respond to the peer reviewing your work.

## Light checking and visible integration

Run a small behavior example plus existing relevant checks. Learn or revisit one short testing pattern when relevant; no testing-only task, dedicated tester, coverage quota, or large test suite. Demonstrate your slice connected to the working product, with honest partial/failure outcomes. Keep the last working flow available.

## Implementation acceptance

- [ ] My named owned unit meets the original input/output, error, validation-order, and mutation contract.
- [ ] Its relevant normal/failure examples work in the integrated product.
- [ ] I reviewed the assigned peer, responded to implementation findings, and recorded the actual revision/checks and their limits.

Close this implementation issue when that bounded work is accepted. Follow your own previous-day issue chain; a later task is not a substitute for a missing predecessor. Do not auto-close another learner's issue.
